habit_scope: 2-story light-wood SFR. WRB (building paper or housewrap) over wall sheathing, then water-impermeable sill/pan, then window, then head flashing, then cladding. CMHC Ch13–15 Fig 130; AF&PA Type 15 felt. Not FM 5-426 hasty sash. Not EIFS. Canadian NBC labeled — confirm AHJ.
how_it_is_done: Roof covering on so the house is dry-in (CMHC Ch15: windows usually after framing and roof covering; Ch2: Doors and Windows after Framing). Logan ice barrier is P09, not this phase. Fontana does not get a Utah snow pack.

Wall sheathing already on (P08). Plywood/OSB usually vertical, 2–3 mm (1/8 in) gap, edge nails 150 mm (6 in) OC, field 300 mm (12 in) OC, 10 mm (3/8 in) min edge distance (CMHC Fig 107). Closer nailing for high wind/earthquake — confirm AHJ. This nailing is the sheathing already filed on P08; P10 does not re-nail it as a new habit.

Sheathing membrane (WRB) over the sheathing. CMHC Ch13 CLASSes: (1) building paper, bituminous-impregnated, 915 mm (36 in) rolls, horizontal strips starting at the bottom, stapled, each strip shingle-lapped over the one beneath; (2) spun-bonded polyolefin (SBPO / Housewrap), rolls 2.74 m (9 ft) by up to 45 m (150 ft), horizontal strips covering a storey height, stapled, strong enough to turn into openings; (3) self-adhesive peel-and-stick in 915 mm (36 in) rolls at door/window sills and heads and other high-water areas. AF&PA (US): siding and exterior trim over Type 15 asphalt felt or other water-repellent sheathing cover. Label: CMHC paper/SBPO is Canadian NBC language; AF&PA Type 15 felt is the US book CLASS. Confirm AHJ. Do not invent a brand. AF&PA Building or Sheathing Paper: Type 15 asphalt-saturated felt or other water-repellent paper/film, vapor permeability ≥5; applied from the bottom; horizontal joints lapped 4 in, vertical joints 6 in; 6-in wide strips around all wall openings and behind all exterior trim (Figs 54–55).

Window sequence CMHC Fig 130 (must keep order): A1 sub-sill slope to exterior; A2 sheathing membrane below the opening; A3 water-impermeable (WI) sill membrane; A4 WI corner reinforcement membrane; B5 overlapping WI membrane; C6 vertical sheathing membrane wrapped into the side of the window; C7 horizontal sheathing membrane wrapped under the header; D8 install window, shims and insulation; D9 head flashing; D10 install and lap wall sheathing membrane; D11 lap sheathing membrane above the opening; E12 wood furring; E13 metal drip edge; E14 siding (P11); E15 backer rod and exterior and interior sealants.

CMHC Ch14: flashing over windows and doors (head/drip flashing) unless protected by an overhang — required when the vertical distance from window/door to underside of overhang is more than one-quarter the horizontal projection (example: flashing required if top of window is more than 300 mm / 12 in below a 1.2 m / 4 ft eave). Head flashing extends from the top of the window/door up and under the sheathing paper or membrane. If sills are not self-flashing, flashing between underside of window/door and the wall below. Fig 125: end dam; solder or sealant at joints; counter flashing mechanically fastened to sheathing with flat-head galvanized roofing nails at 300 mm (12 in) OC, min two per segment.

Install windows plumb and level in the rough opening using shims (CMHC Ch15). Fig 132: RO 25 mm (1 in) larger than outside of window frame for a minimum 12.5 mm (1/2 in) space; attach with wood screws through the sides of the window frame only; shims at jamb and sill junctions only; shim at junction of multiple units; fill from the inside with foam insulation OR insulate and air-seal. Always refer to manufacturer's instructions. Air barrier at the interior edge so incidental leakage drains out. Closed-cell sprayed foam is named as a one-step insulate-and-air-seal after the window is in — in higher exposure, interior sealant plus drainable insulation is preferred.

Sill (Fig 131): 25 mm (1 in) extension beyond cladding or inner face of masonry sill; 6% slope; drip notch 6 mm (1/4 in) beyond cladding or 15 mm (5/8 in) beyond inner face of masonry sill; water-impermeable membrane over sloped sub-sill or over horizontal sill with dam.
Store windows upright, dry, level, original packaging, temporary bracing left in place. Remove/label/store screens until construction is complete (CMHC Ch15).
FM 5-426 Ch8 OPENED: double-hung sash, millwork frames, hasty openings with stops nailed to the stud. Silent on WRB, pan, end-dam, housewrap. Do not file as this habit.
Essential Guide to Framing OPENED: window/door headers and corner-window clips — framing, not WRB. HUD RSDG OPENED: wind/C&C loads on windows, not a flashing SOP.
trades: building official (framing inspection including windows/doors/skylights — CMHC Ch2)
tools_equipment: Named: shims; wood screws; staples; backer rod; sealant; spray foam CLASS; manufacturer tools. Not a SKU list.
inspection_hold_points: WRB in place and shingle-lapped before cladding (CMHC Ch13; AF&PA Type 15 felt).
Fig 130 order: sill membrane and corner reinforcement BEFORE the window; head flashing then membrane lap above AFTER the window.
End dam at flashing joints (Fig 125). Solder or sealant at joints.
Window plumb and level; screws through jambs only (Fig 132). Manufacturer instructions.
Head flashing unless the overhang rule is met (Ch14).
Contact building official to inspect completed framing including windows, doors and skylights (CMHC Ch2). No skip-inspection.
material_classes: spun-bonded polyolefin housewrap CLASS — CMHC Canadian
typical_duration_sfr: CMHC Ch2: installing doors and windows requires a few days — Canadian sample, not a Utah/Fontana cycle. Do not invent lag days.
when_this_beats_habit: This is the habit. EIFS is an alt (m-P11-eifs), not a WRB skip.
when_this_is_a_bad_idea: Installing the window before the sill membrane. Skipping end-dams. Copying Canadian poly as the WRB. Selling a brand housewrap as the only CLASS. Using FM 5-426 hasty sash as SFR WRB. Inventing IRC pan sections.
why_tier1_never_learned_it: They hang windows. What they skip is Fig 130 order: pan and corners before the unit, head flash then membrane lap above after, screws through jambs only, end-dams.
permit_gate: should be on drawings before permit
permit_gate_notes: Fenestration ratings (CMHC names NAFS/NBC — Canadian). US: confirm AHJ energy/egress. Do not invent IRC section numbers. Title 24 is P13 Fontana hold, not this flashing SOP.
risk_if_swapped_late: Changing WRB type or pan detail after openings are cut is a leak callback, not a field save. Catch before windows land.
plain_language_summary: Paper or housewrap on the sheathing, starting at the bottom, each row lapped like a shingle. Pan the sill and the corners before the window goes in. Screw the window through the sides only. Head flash, then lap the wrap over that flashing. End-dams at the corners. Do not invent a brand wrap.
spanish_summary: Papel o housewrap sobre el forro, de abajo hacia arriba, cada tira traslapada. Charola en el alfeizar y las esquinas ANTES de la ventana. Tornillos solo por los lados. Flash de cabeza, luego el wrap encima. End-dams. No invente una marca.

labor_notes: Do not invent crew counts. Manufacturer instructions named.
layering: Fig 130 order is the layering. Sill membrane and corners BEFORE the unit. Head flashing then membrane lap above AFTER the unit.
AF&PA WRB: from the bottom; 4 in horizontal lap; 6 in vertical lap; 6-in strips at openings and behind exterior trim. Perm ≥5 — this paper is not the interior vapor retarder.
Sheathing membrane shingle-lapped; start at the bottom of the wall (CMHC Ch13).
RO 1 in larger than the frame; 1/2 in min space (Fig 132).
Sill: 6% slope; 1 in extension; drip notch (Fig 131).
AF&PA: siding/trim ≥6 in above finished grade (Fig 54). CMHC siding ≥200 mm (8 in) from ground — CANADIAN, confirm AHJ. Do not copy 8 in as Utah/Fontana without AHJ.
code_to_check: AHJ flashing/WRB. CMHC is NBC — not IRC. Do not invent R703.
NAFS/NBC fenestration is Canadian — confirm US AHJ energy/egress. Title 24 is P13 Fontana, not this SOP.
time_money: CMHC: a few days for doors and windows. No dollars. Late WRB/pan swap is a leak, not a save.

walkthroughs.title: How to Flash a Window in Tar Paper
walkthroughs.what_it_shows: Field custom house: two-layer #30 felt WRB + fluid pan CLASS + drip cap + second-layer lap. End-dams and 2-story not spoken. Fast Flash is CLASS, not a brand habit. Do not invent IRC. Hunt cw-P10-2026-08-30.

images.caption: CMHC Fig 130 Sequence for window installation (printed p 179): sub-sill slope; membrane below; WI sill + corners; vertical wrap into sides; window/shims; head flashing; lap membrane above; furring; drip; siding; backer rod and sealants. Canadian NBC — confirm AHJ.
CMHC Fig 107 panel sheathing 6 in edge / 12 in field, 1/8 in gap, 3/8 in min edge distance (printed p 149). Sheathing is P08; this page is the substrate the WRB goes on.

inspector_looks_for: WRB shingle-lapped, started at the bottom (CMHC Ch13).
Sill/pan and corner membrane before the window (Fig 130).
Head flashing then membrane lap above the opening (Fig 130 / Ch14).
End dams; joints soldered or sealed (Fig 125).
Framing inspection includes windows/doors/skylights (CMHC Ch2). No skip-inspection.
AF&PA 4 in horiz / 6 in vert laps; 6-in strips at openings (Figs 54–55).
do_not_cheap: Pan and corner membrane BEFORE the window (Fig 130 hold).
Head flashing up and under the WRB (Ch14 hold).
Do not skip the framing inspection that includes windows (Ch2). No skip-inspection.
AF&PA 4 in horizontal / 6 in vertical WRB laps; 6-in strips at openings (layering).
smart_save: Closed-cell spray foam named as one-step insulate-and-air-seal after the window is in — not a pan skip. Higher exposure: drainable insulation + interior sealant. No dollars.
Late swap of WRB/pan after the unit is in is a leak callback.
